correctness.rationale: With the directed pure neighborhood rule the hub distance is zero and leaf i tests its deviation from the mean of all leaves, independent of the hub. If no leaf lies at the mean, split the leaves below and above it with counts a,b and group means L,U. The least deviation is at most both group-average deviations, b(U−L)/k and a(U−L)/k; U−L≤1 gives the bound floor(k/2)/k. The balanced endpoint profile attains it and the strict test closes every leaf gate at equality. On this frozen profile the hub is an affine iteration driven by iid Bernoulli(p) leaf selections. For 0<ρ≤1/2 the two images cover the unit interval; all length-n images cover it and shrink uniformly. Every word recurs infinitely often on one full-probability event, so arbitrary neighborhoods are visited infinitely often. At half compromise the recent M bits approximate the hub by at most 2^(−M); empirical block probabilities converge by the strong law on disjoint blocks, giving weak empirical convergence. Binary digit frequencies distinguish the odd-degree measure from Lebesgue measure, dyadic cylinder log masses converge to the binary entropy exponent, and typical-set covering and the dyadic mass-distribution bound give the Hausdorff dimension. Positive cylinders give full support and shrinking cylinder masses give no atoms. A fresh rational replay checked 19,525 grid profiles for k=2,…,6, exact boundary transitions and finite affine-image coverage, without substituting for any infinite-path argument.
residual_risks: Temporal independence is an explicit assumption of this theorem; the inspected primary sampling text confirms the single-edge subcase but does not explicitly state independence between steps.
No general consensus threshold, general-graph claim, or odd/even occupation classification for other frozen profiles is asserted.

evidence: The general NDW primary passage specifies directed gates and allows single-edge sampling. The binary-star theorem explicitly excludes arbitrary initial leaf opinions; the mixed-confidence theorem is on a three-vertex path.

originality.rationale: The closest indexed binary-star result covers the canonical binary thresholds, the exact recursion, and the entropy law in degree at least three; the aligned three-vertex records add overlap at degree two. The recursion also makes the stated full interval and empirical refinements accessible by standard iid word arguments. The distinct structural statement is the sharp existence threshold across all real-valued leaf vectors: the prior binary-profile analysis establishes attainability but not the universal upper bound against every nonbinary vector. The arbitrary-profile extremal bound is part of the original finding, not a new repair. Credit the overlapping dynamical consequences and classical dimension law rather than treating them as independently novel. This is a bounded coverage judgment, not historical priority.
residual_risks: The inspections are bounded; catalogue dates and overlap do not establish discovery order. The entropy law itself is classical, and the binary-star dynamical overlap is substantial.

value.rationale: The universal initial-profile bound answers a natural extremal question for a basic network class: whether any genuinely nonbinary arrangement can sustain complete structural leaf unreceptivity above the balanced-endpoint value. It also isolates what the threshold does not say about consensus. The construction demonstrates endogenous persistent fluctuations from asymmetric confidence tests without artificial stubborn agents; in its canonical odd-degree case full path density is compatible with a singular time-occupation measure. The dichotomy illustrates the boundary and is not presented as a new theorem about Bernoulli measures.
residual_risks: The threshold concerns complete structural unreceptivity, not eventual consensus, convergence from generic states, or parity effects for arbitrary leaf balances.
